constraints: Pure refactor; every existing test name and assertion is kept; the 17 parity blocks only move and are still collected by bun test apps/cli/src.

New modules have no module-level side effects other than constants; no regex splitting of long strings, deep recursion, per-operation closures or handler tables (the native CLI runs the code in Boa). harness.ts does no file system access at import time.

Load-tolerant gates (design D11): mise run verify and mise run test-cli run only inside the design's three-attempt sh -c loops; command 10 runs directly after the test-cli loop. If all three attempts fail, the gate fails; it is never waived as load.

Every verification command exits 0 with tests actually run once its plan's changes are in; native parity is verified only through mise run test-cli; block presence and names are checked statically (D13).

Every plan declares artifactRoots ["target"]; every file a plan edits is in its writePaths (docs/development.md for sms-02 only if a review finding concerns its edit sentences; apps/cli/native/README.md for sms-03).
Strictly typed code in the surrounding style; no emojis; cargo with CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true; no tool attribution in commits.
designDecisionsAndRationale: D1-D12 reused (class chain, component members in Editor, lowest-chain-class planner types, Batch class with module-level handlers and the switch in Batch.apply, parity topic files with a non-test harness, focused tests only for newly extracted helpers, load-tolerant gates).

Expected test counts are pinned (2956, 183, 11); a review correction that adds tests raises them by exactly that number and the progress log records why.
If the 0.8.5 reference binary is missing, workers stop with a blocker and the orchestrator builds the b52e4db reference; workers never create git worktrees.

Every edit failure path keeps the same error message and the same first failing check, including the unknown-op error from the switch in Batch.apply.
A test-cli or verify attempt that fails on deadlines under load is retried by the loop; the count checks read only the green copy; a third failure is a hard gate failure.
